title: PlayZone VIP | Sebastian Sanchez
description: Case study for PlayZone VIP, a client web application built and deployed with Next.js, TypeScript, and responsive design.
ogDescription: A production client web application built with Next.js, TypeScript, JavaScript, HTML, and CSS.
name: PlayZone VIP
headline: A production website for turning a brand idea into a usable experience.
summary: PlayZone VIP was a freelance project where the challenge was not just building an interface, but turning business requirements into a clear, responsive, production-ready web experience.

problem.title: The problem
problem.body: The client needed a web presence that communicated the brand, worked well on mobile, and could be deployed without becoming hard to maintain.
points: Turn business requirements into a concrete interface.
Keep the experience clear across desktop and mobile.
Ship to production with a simple foundation that could evolve.

role.title: My role
role.body: I handled frontend development, responsive adaptation, project structure, and deployment. It was an end-to-end execution job: understand what the client needed, build it, and leave it running in production.

sections.title: Goal
sections.body: Translate a business need into a website that felt direct, navigable, and ready for real users.
points: Prioritize simple navigation and scannable content.
Avoid unnecessary complexity to keep the project agile.

sections.title: Execution
sections.body: I built the interface with Next.js and TypeScript, taking care of structure, styling, mobile adaptation, and deployment. The focus was keeping the product understandable, stable, and easy to adjust.
points: Organized components and styles to make changes easier.
Responsive design for different screen sizes.
Visual detail review before moving to production.
Final deployment and follow-up adjustments based on client needs.

sections.title: Challenges
sections.body: In a freelance project, the technical challenge is mixed with communication, timing, and practical decisions. The goal was to ship something polished without overdesigning it.
points: Make visual and technical decisions with incomplete information.
Keep scope controlled enough to reach production.

sections.title: Learning
sections.body: This project reinforced the importance of communicating tradeoffs clearly, moving with real constraints, and closing the loop all the way to production.
points: A project is not done when it compiles; it is done when it is published and serves its goal.
Simple structure is often better than heavy architecture for a client website.
Responsive design is not an extra; it is central to the experience.

next.title: Next
next.body: Polish the case study with real screenshots, visual decisions, and a more detailed read of the deployment process.
